note: Cognitive demand, curriculum stage and author-anticipated challenge are separate descriptors, not student-tested difficulty metrics. Each task maps to a proposed mathematics prerequisite graph.

tasks.cohort: secondary learners who have studied quadratic equations
targetPrerequisites: sign logic of two real roots
tasks.challengeRationale: Several individually familiar strict conditions must be combined and an unjustified sufficient-condition shortcut avoided.
tasks.verifiedResult: For x^2 - 2ax + a + 2 = 0, two distinct positive real roots iff a > 2. The discriminant condition alone is a < -1 or a > 2; root sum 2a > 0, product a+2 > 0.
validAlternativeMethods: sign analysis of roots using quadratic formula
tasks.risk: An answer-only comparison may overlook whether the learner understands necessity versus sufficiency.

tasks.challengeRationale: Requires distinguishing unconditional from conditioned events, then representing the eligible unordered pairs consistently.
tasks.verifiedResult: From 5 red and 4 blue without replacement, P(both red | at least one red)=C(5,2)/(C(9,2)-C(4,2))=10/30=1/3. For 3 draws the analogous numerator C(5,3), denominator C(9,3)-C(4,3).
tasks.risk: A numerical answer can be correct while denominator reasoning or the conditioning interpretation remains unsupported.

tasks.cohort: upper primary learners working with unlike denominators
tasks.challengeRationale: Requires keeping the referent whole fixed and rewriting unequal-sized parts as common units.
validAlternativeMethods: area or strip model with common twelfths
tasks.risk: Correcting the number without repairing the student's unit model.

tasks.cohort: lower secondary learners studying percent changes
tasks.challengeRationale: The second relative change applies to the new amount, not the original base.
tasks.verifiedResult: Starting at 200, a 20% increase yields 240, then a 20% decrease gives 192: 96% of the starting amount, a net 4% decrease.
tasks.risk: Treating equal percentage changes as inverse additive effects.

tasks.challengeRationale: Cancelling a factor is only equivalent where the denominator is defined; the apparent solution is excluded.
tasks.verifiedResult: (x^2-1)/(x-1)=2 requires x!=1. Simplifying gives x+1=2 and candidate x=1, excluded. The equation has no solution.
tasks.risk: Accepting an excluded root after a valid-looking algebraic cancellation.

tasks.cohort: secondary learners studying composite functions and radicals
tasks.challengeRationale: Requires preserving inner and outer domain restrictions; the two composition orders have different domains.
tasks.verifiedResult: f(x)=sqrt(x-1), g(x)=x^2. Domain of f∘g is (-infinity,-1] U [1,infinity); domain of g∘f is [1,infinity).
validAlternativeMethods: evaluate inner function then outer function
tasks.risk: Losing the negative-x branch in f(g(x)) or assuming domain is commutative.

targetPrerequisites: decreasing logarithms for bases between 0 and 1
tasks.challengeRationale: Combines the logarithm domain and decreasing monotonicity, with strict inequality at the endpoint.
tasks.risk: Using increasing-monotonicity inequality direction or forgetting x>1.

tasks.cohort: lower secondary learners studying similar triangles
tasks.challengeRationale: Similarity affects two independent linear dimensions in an area measure.
tasks.verifiedResult: If corresponding sides have scale 3/2, areas have scale (3/2)^2=9/4, not 3/2.
tasks.risk: Accepting a linear factor as the area factor.

tasks.cohort: upper secondary learners using coordinate geometry and circle-line intersections
tasks.challengeRationale: Every line in the family meets a fixed circle point; only one slope yields a single intersection.
tasks.verifiedResult: Circle x^2+y^2=25 and line y=mx+5 give x((1+m^2)x+10m)=0. Distinct intersections unless m=0, when x=0 is a double root; tangency iff m=0.
tasks.risk: Mistaking a line through a circle point for a tangent without checking the second intersection.

tasks.cohort: secondary learners studying counting with repeated symbols
tasks.challengeRationale: Physical tiles can differ without making resulting letter strings distinct; category counts matter.
tasks.verifiedResult: Choosing and ordering 3 tiles from A,A,B,B gives exactly AAB, ABA, BAA, ABB, BAB, BBA: 6 distinct length-3 strings.
validAlternativeMethods: count 3 arrangements for each of AAB and ABB
tasks.risk: Applying 4P3 counts distinct tiles as distinct letters, overcounting visible results.

tasks.cohort: upper secondary learners familiar with conditional probability
tasks.challengeRationale: The screening sensitivity is not the posterior defect rate because nondefective items dominate the population.
tasks.verifiedResult: Defect prior=0.01, sensitivity=0.90, false positive=0.05; P(defect | positive)=0.009/(0.009+0.0495)=2/13 (~15.38%).
validAlternativeMethods: 10000-item frequency table (90 true positives and 495 false positives)

tasks.cohort: secondary or introductory statistics learners comparing stratified success rates
tasks.challengeRationale: Within-stratum comparisons reverse after pooling because strategies have very different group weights.
tasks.verifiedResult: Small group A 9/10 vs B 80/100; large group A 20/100 vs B 1/10. A wins within both groups (90%>80%, 20%>10%) yet pooled A=29/110 (~26.4%) < B=81/110 (~73.6%) due to unequal group mixtures.
tasks.risk: Claiming subgroup advantage guarantees pooled advantage or that pooled comparison alone determines a fair treatment effect.

tasks.cohort: advanced secondary learners beginning proof by induction
tasks.challengeRationale: A formula can fit initial examples but still require induction to justify every positive integer n.
tasks.risk: Treating checks n=1,2,3 as a proof for every n or over-explaining despite partial valid work.

tasks.cohort: upper secondary learners using AM-GM and universal quantifiers
tasks.challengeRationale: A valid inequality on x>0 is falsely generalized to every nonzero real x.
tasks.verifiedResult: For x>0, x+1/x >= 2 with equality at x=1 by AM-GM. For x<0, x+1/x <= -2, so x=-1 gives -2<2: statement for all x≠0 is false.
tasks.risk: Rewarding a proof applied outside its domain or hiding the equality case.

tasks.cohort: introductory calculus learners optimizing polynomial functions on closed intervals
tasks.challengeRationale: Two stationary points and two endpoints must all be considered, including ties; interior derivative-zero is not sufficient.
tasks.verifiedResult: For f(x)=x^3-3x on [-2,2], f'(x)=3x²-3, critical x=±1; f(-2)=-2,f(-1)=2,f(1)=-2,f(2)=2. Global maxima 2 at x=-1 and x=2; minima -2 at x=-2 and x=1.
validAlternativeMethods: monotonic interval analysis with endpoint evaluation
tasks.risk: Announcing a unique maximum from f'=0 while neglecting endpoint ties.

tasks.cohort: introductory linear algebra learners interpreting linear systems
tasks.challengeRationale: Dependent coefficients alone do not guarantee infinitely many solutions; the right-hand sides may conflict.
tasks.verifiedResult: System x+2y=3 and 2x+4y=7 is inconsistent (doubling first gives 2x+4y=6, not 7); coefficient rank=1 and augmented rank=2.
validAlternativeMethods: double first equation and compare constants
tasks.risk: Equating determinant zero with infinitely many solutions instead of zero or infinitely many.
